s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic testicular swelling with acute worsening and a palpable mass
salient_findings: Left testicular bloating and dull pain for 20 years
Acute worsening over the past 10 days
Enlarged, firm, smooth left testis without discrete nodules or tenderness
Negative transillumination
Well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow on scrotal Doppler ultrasound
key_facts: 49-year-old man
Left testicular bloating and dull pain for 20 years
Acute worsening over the past 10 days
Denied other medical history
Left testis was enlarged, firm, smooth, without discrete nodules or tenderness
Transillumination was negative
Right testis, epididymides, and vas deferens were normal
Scrotal Doppler ultrasound showed bilateral epididymal cysts
1.09 × 0.79 cm well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow
Small left hydrocele
Serum CA19-9 level of 57.5 U/mL (normal <27 U/mL)
Alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin, and other tumor markers were within normal limits

differentials: Malignant mesothelioma of the tunica vaginalis
per_call: Malignant mesothelioma of the tunica vaginalis

shortlist.label: Seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Leading clinical consideration with a well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion in the left testis and internal blood flow

shortlist.label: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the acute worsening of testicular swelling and elevated CA19-9 level

shortlist.label: Mixed sex cord-stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the presence of a palpable mass and abnormal ultrasound findings

shortlist.label: Leydig cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the firm and smooth nature of the left testis

shortlist.label: Sertoli cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the presence of a well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion and abnormal CA19-9 level

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow and elevated serum CA19-9 level, along with normal alpha-fetoprotein and human chorionic gonadotropin levels, suggests a seminoma, which is a type of germ cell tumor.

rejected.label: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
rejected.why: Normal alpha-fetoprotein and human chorionic gonadotropin levels make this less likely

rejected.label: Mixed sex cord-stromal tumor
rejected.why: The ultrasound findings and tumor markers do not specifically suggest this diagnosis

rejected.label: Leydig cell tumor
rejected.why: Typically presents with hormonal symptoms and has different ultrasound characteristics

rejected.label: Sertoli cell tumor
rejected.why: Less common and does not typically present with the described ultrasound and laboratory findings
